independence_declaration.statement:
I am code-security-reviewer, session 5764bad1-1f26-4ae5-907d-11c9c87bad9d, task T-DG7-REV-CS-RG3. I verified the assignment's SHA-256 (9ef6c1c51a74a25e1eb339c2f3904e2f471d6c040eee50ffc9899272497a985c).

I authored no implementation in the DG7 scope. P7 and its repairs (DO-D11, DO-D12, DO-D13 by devops-engineer; SA-ADR71, SA-ADR72 by solution-architect; AN-P7J by transformation-analyst) were built by implementer roles. qa-verifier wrote the pre-freeze acceptance tests, and delivery-orchestrator integrated the work and ran the host drills.

I formed this verdict without opening any other reviewer's round-3 record or evidence. I read my own role's round-2 record and findings to verify F-DG7-1041, and the QA round-2 A19 restore report (a previous round's evidence) only for its R7 count.

HEAD at the start was 557a95133. The only commit after source_commit 3e8f5bce2 touches the three round-3 assignments, the frozen manifest and stages.json, all excluded from the candidate. The candidate id was recomputed and matches; see SEC-RG3-00.

Three inconsistencies in the assignment are reported, not followed:
- It asks for `round: 7`, but the record path is round-3, and tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs l.682/794 requires rec.round to equal the round directory and the stages.json round entry. This record says round 3.
- It names docs/delivery/reviews/DG5/round-7/code-security-reviewer.json as the field-set template. I mirrored my role's DG7 round-2 record, which has the schema's full property set.
- It says candidate.mjs counts 3158 files. The tool and the frozen manifest both give 3160 entries. The id matches, so this is a stale count in the assignment, not a candidate difference.

This review is engineering evidence only. It grants no business, Finance or IT approval. Product gate G6 does not imply DG7, and DG7 implies no G1-G6 approval.

checks_run.environment: Live repository, read-only; Node v24.21.0 (/opt/nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin first on PATH).
checks_run.expected: candidate sha256:cf1fb7d59a04e2f0d18a7773eca4e10893b72f3119a70d0e74796c8a8437a541; the commits after the source commit change only metadata.
checks_run.actual:
HEAD is 557a95133, the round-3 freeze commit. It changes only the three round-3 assignments, candidates/DG7/cf1fb7d59a04e2f0.manifest.json and stages.json, all META_EXCLUDES of tools/gates/lib/candidate.mjs.

candidate.mjs gives sha256:cf1fb7d59a04e2f0d18a7773eca4e10893b72f3119a70d0e74796c8a8437a541 over 3160 files for the working tree, --ref 3e8f5bce and --ref HEAD (all exit 0). --diff gives matches: true, with added, removed and changed all empty. The manifest has 3160 entries; the assignment's '3158 files' is stale.

I executed code only in a disposable `git clone --shared` sparse clone at 3e8f5bce under $TMPDIR. It excluded docs/delivery/{runs,test-evidence,handbacks} and trading_agent/, because a full clone hit ENOSPC on the shared volume and its partial checkout was deleted at once. The clone's own candidate.mjs --ref HEAD also gave cf1fb7d5. Gate validators and read-only scans were also run on the live tree where noted.

checks_run.environment: Disposable clone at 3e8f5bce; node_modules symlinked read-only from the repository; Node v24.21.0.

I reviewed the mount change itself. The whole deploy/compose directory is now mounted read-only into the backup container, adding compose.load.yaml, compose.no-egress.yaml, db-init/ and .env. checks_run.procedure: Probe the F-DG7-1053 repair beyond the shipped tests. An accepted root reaches the DATABASE_URL check, and a refused one fails earlier.
checks_run.command: bash deploy/scripts/backup.sh --out <root> --label probe, with DATABASE_URL unset, for 7 roots: link to 0700; link to 1777; the same with a trailing '/'; a relative link to 1777; a 1777 dir with '/'; a link to a 0700 dir under a 0777 parent; link/.
checks_run.environment: Disposable clone; scratch directories under $TMPDIR; uid 0 (find -perm judges modes regardless of uid).
checks_run.expected: Writable targets refused (exit 2, naming the target), owner-only targets accepted, nothing created.
checks_run.actual:
Every case behaves as ADR-0066 A1.3 states.
- Links to 1777 targets, relative links and trailing-slash forms are refused (exit 2); the trailing-slash form is judged through the link by find.
- 0700 targets are accepted: each reaches 'BLOCKED: DATABASE_URL … is not set', which is also exit 2, by design of the probe.
- No file was created under any root.
- The link to a 0700 dir under a 0777 parent is accepted. That is residual 7 (ancestors are not checked), which is disclosed.

summary:
FAIL on sha256:cf1fb7d5.

F-DG7-1041 (mine) is CLOSED_VERIFIED: ADR-0063 Amendment 2 and ADR-0066 Amendment 1 now state the DO-D11 behaviour exactly as built.

This round's code repairs are sound:
- the DO-D12 symlink root (18/18 tests, plus a 7-case probe);
- the DO-D13 mounts and preflight (12/12);
- DATABASE_URL_FILE in the CLI (15/15; fails closed, leaks nothing);
- import-findings REOPENED to OPEN, and the 3-4 digit id pattern (probed);
- the history allow-list entry: sha256('[masked]'), history-only, not a credential.
The secret, claims, no-CDN and seal scans and tests pass. The release-tool failures were all environmental and re-ran green. The asset scan is BLOCKED in my environment (source-map host paths from symlinked node_modules); its inputs are unchanged since round 2.

Three new findings, none Critical, High or mandatory:
- F-DG7-1071 (Medium): in the phased Compose backup the manifest's config.files is always empty, because --phase finish reads config.sha from the database phase's deleted temp directory. Reproduced on PostgreSQL; it is the unexplained 'cat: … config.sha' error line in drill rg3b C5.
- F-DG7-1072 (Medium): the only Compose A19 drill moved 0 evidence objects and 0 jobs. The DO-D13 DAC_READ_SEARCH repair and the evidence and job legs of the Compose restore are therefore undemonstrated, and D-284 does not disclose this.
- F-DG7-1073 (Low): ADR-0066 is not amended for DO-D13 (the capability grant, DATABASE_URL_FILE, the /mth layout), DO-D13 Q2 is unanswered, and the allow-list cites a non-existent D-285.
The two Medium findings must be repaired before the gate (D-192), so the verdict is FAIL.

This record grants no business, Finance or IT approval and does not imply DG7.
